newsitem.title: CONGO: S.Africa says Zaire peace talks postoned.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa says Zaire peace talks postoned.

text.p: Talks scheduled for Wednesday between Zairean President Mobutu Sese Seko and rebel leader Laurent Kabila have been postponed, probably till Thursday, the South African Deputy Foreign Minister Aziz Pahad said.
"We are still continuing discussions.... I think we can predict it (the meeting) will start tomorrow," he told reporters aboard the South African ice-breaker Outeniqua, the site of the talks.
Pahad said Kabila had raised last-minute security concerns that forced the delay, insisting the ship should be in international waters and not docked in Pointe Noire when he went aboard.
"We did not expect this as a problem because the President (Nelson Mandela) discussed it last week on several occasions," he said.
A first meeting between Mobutu and Kabila on May 4 ended inconclusively. Mobutu offered to hand power to a transitional authority but Kabila insisted he take power directly.
Kabila's aides said they were going to the second meeting in the expectation that Mobutu, who has lost control of most of Zaire, would comply with their demands.
Mobutu and Mandela, who was scheduled to chair the second meeting, arrived in the Atlantic sea port separately close to the scheduled starting time of 11 a.m. (1000 gmt) and waited ashore.
A rebel official told Reuters by telephone from Cabinda that Kabila insisted on boarding the ship by helicopter in international waters off the Congo coast.
"The president (Kabila) is in Cabinda waiting. He wants to go to the ship but the ship is still in Pointe Noire and it must be in international waters," he said.

Pahad said Mandela, waiting ashore in Pointe Noire with Congolese President Pascal Lissouba, had been in contact with other African leaders as well as the United States and Britain in a bid to bolster the peace process.
Mobutu arrived by air from Kinshasa and spent the day with his own delegation in Pointe Noire.

South African government spokesman Joel Netshitenzhe said on Tuesday that Mandela and Deputy President Thabo Mbeki had hammered out the skeleton of an agreement in telephone talks with Mobutu and Kabila.
